Samitier returned to [Spain](/wiki/Spain "Spain") and became manager of [CF Barcelona](/wiki/CF_Barcelona "CF Barcelona") in 1944. In [1945](/wiki/La_Liga_1944%E2%80%9345 "La Liga 1944–45") he guided them to only their second ever [La Liga](/wiki/La_Liga "La Liga") title. Then they beat the [Copa del Generalísimo](/wiki/Copa_del_General%C3%ADsimo "Copa del Generalísimo") winners [Atlético Bilbao](/wiki/Atl%C3%A9tico_Bilbao "Atlético Bilbao") to win the [Copa de Oro Argentina](/wiki/Copa_de_Oro_Argentina "Copa de Oro Argentina"). Samitier subsequently worked as the clubs *chief scout* and was instrumental in the recruitment of another [CF Barcelona](/wiki/FC_Barcelona "FC Barcelona") legend [Ladislao Kubala](/wiki/Ladislao_Kubala "Ladislao Kubala").

In the summer of 1950 Kubala arrived in [Spain](/wiki/Spain "Spain") with his own team, *Hungaria*. The team was made up of fellow refugees fleeing [Eastern Europe](/wiki/Eastern_Europe "Eastern Europe"). They played a series of friendlies against a *Madrid Select XI*, a [Spain XI](/wiki/Spain_national_football_team "Spain national football team") and [RCD Español](/wiki/RCD_Espa%C3%B1ol "RCD Español"). During these games, Kubala was spotted by both [Real Madrid](/wiki/Real_Madrid "Real Madrid") and Samitier. Kubala was offered a contract by Real but was then persuaded by Samitier to sign for CF Barcelona. It has been suggested that Samitier used his connections within [Francoist Spain](/wiki/Francoist_Spain "Francoist Spain") to help arrange the transfer. In the midst of the [Cold War](/wiki/Cold_War "Cold War"), Kubala's escape to the West was used by [Francoist Spain](/wiki/Francoist_Spain "Francoist Spain") and was made into a film *The Stars Search for Peace* which saw Kubala and Samitier playing themselves.

Bathroom facilities for women in the Senate on the [Senate chamber](/wiki/United_States_Capitol "United States Capitol") level were first provided in 1992.[[9]](#cite_note-Plaskow-10) Women were not allowed to wear pants on the Senate floor until 1993.[[10]](#cite_note-chicagotribune2004-11)[[11]](#cite_note-rollcall1-12) In 1993, Senators [Barbara Mikulski](/wiki/Barbara_Mikulski "Barbara Mikulski") and [Carol Moseley Braun](/wiki/Carol_Moseley_Braun "Carol Moseley Braun") wore pants onto the floor in defiance of the rule, and female support staff followed soon after, with the rule being amended later that year by Senate Sergeant-at-Arms Martha Pope to allow women to wear pants on the floor so long as they also wore a jacket.[[10]](#cite_note-chicagotribune2004-11)[[11]](#cite_note-rollcall1-12)

The first time two female senators from the same state served concurrently was in 1993; [Dianne Feinstein](/wiki/Dianne_Feinstein "Dianne Feinstein") and [Barbara Boxer](/wiki/Barbara_Boxer "Barbara Boxer") of California were both elected in 1992, with Feinstein taking office that same year (as the result of a special election) and Boxer taking office in 1993. Boxer served until 2016, when she retired, and Feinstein was then joined by [Kamala Harris](/wiki/Kamala_Harris "Kamala Harris"). In June 1993, [Kay Bailey Hutchison](/wiki/Kay_Bailey_Hutchison "Kay Bailey Hutchison") won a special election in Texas, and joined Kassebaum as a fellow female [Republican](/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)") senator. These additions significantly diminished the popular perception of the Senate as an exclusive "boys' club". Since 1992, there has been at least one new woman elected to the Senate every two years, with the exception of [2004](/wiki/2004_United_States_Senate_elections "2004 United States Senate elections") (Lisa Murkowski was elected for the first time in 2004, but had been appointed to the seat since 2002).

Apple's world corporate headquarters are located in [Cupertino](/wiki/Cupertino "Cupertino"), in the middle of California's [Silicon Valley](/wiki/Silicon_Valley "Silicon Valley"), at Apple Park, a massive circular [groundscraper](/wiki/Groundscraper "Groundscraper") building with a [circumference](/wiki/Circumference "Circumference") of one mile (1.6 km). Apple co-founder [Steve Jobs](/wiki/Steve_Jobs "Steve Jobs") wanted Apple Park to look less like a [business park](/wiki/Business_park "Business park") and more like a nature refuge, and personally appeared before the Cupertino City Council in June 2011 to make the proposal, in his final public appearance before his death.

Apple also operates from the Apple Campus (also known by its address, 1 Infinite Loop), a grouping of six buildings in Cupertino that total 850,000 square feet (79,000 m2) located about 1 mile (1.6 km) to the west of Apple Park.[[316]](#cite_note-316) The Apple Campus was the company's headquarters from its opening in 1993, until the opening of Apple Park in 2017.
